title: What is the Reflection API?
keyPoints: Reflection lets you inspect and modify classes, methods, fields, and constructors at runtime
You can create objects, invoke methods, and access private fields dynamically
Used by frameworks: Spring (DI), JPA (entity mapping), JUnit (test discovery), Jackson (JSON binding)
Slower than direct access (~10x) and bypasses compile-time type checking

s1_definition.oneliner: Reflection lets you inspect and manipulate classes, fields, and methods at runtime without knowing them at compile time. Frameworks like Spring and JPA depend on it.
s1_definition.profdef:
Reflection capabilities:

- **Inspect:** Get class name, fields, methods, annotations, constructors at runtime.
- **Create:** Instantiate objects by class name without knowing the type at compile time.
- **Invoke:** Call methods dynamically, including private ones.
- **Access:** Read and write field values, even private fields via `setAccessible(true)`.
s1_definition.analogy: Reflection is like a bank auditor who can open any drawer (private field), read any form (method), and start any procedure (invoke) without needing pre-arranged access. Powerful but risky – it bypasses normal security checks.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Reflection API:
    Class.forName("Account")     → get Class object
    clazz.getDeclaredFields()    → inspect fields
    clazz.getMethod("getBalance") → get Method object
    method.invoke(account)       → call the method
    field.setAccessible(true)    → bypass private
    ctor.newInstance(args)       → create object

  Used by: Spring, JPA, Jackson, JUnit
  Downside: slow, no compile-time safety, breaks encapsulation
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The Reflection API lets you inspect and manipulate classes, fields, methods, and constructors at runtime. You can create objects, invoke methods, and access private fields dynamically without knowing the types at compile time.

Frameworks like Spring, JPA, Jackson, and JUnit depend heavily on reflection. But it is slower than direct access, bypasses compile-time type checking, and can break encapsulation. Java modules restrict deep reflection for security.

One sentence to remember: reflection inspects and manipulates classes at runtime – frameworks depend on it, but it is slow and bypasses safety.
